objective: Cheapest falsification test for dir:llm_8k_gdelt_sentiment_acceleration (registry: reports/research/harvest/directions.jsonl, status=harvested/triaged, verdict='the cheapest possible falsification test with zero new data'): reproduce ONLY the sent_accel feature construction from the LLM_Alpha repo (rank of short-MA(5) minus long-MA(20) of polarity*magnitude, Alpha101-style, EMP2018-attributed negation) on our own 8-K text (reusing the h20260922_01_earnings_text pipeline's raw text and neutralisation code) plus Alpaca/Benzinga news_packets, scored via DeepSeek in place of the source's Claude Haiku 4.5, for one recent complete quarter (2026 Q2, 2026-04-01..2026-06-30) on the tickers with an 8-K in that quarter. Compute daily cross-sectional rank IC against next-5-trading-day returns and a shuffled-news-across-tickers-within-date placebo BEFORE building any purge(5)+embargo(5) walk-forward CV harness. No backtest, no portfolio construction, no CV harness in this pilot.
target_regime_and_horizon: One recent complete quarter, 2026-04-01..2026-06-30 (2026 Q3 is not yet complete as of 2026-09-28 and would need forward returns into October, so Q2 is the most recent fully computable quarter). Universe: tickers with >=1 8-K filing in that quarter in data/features/earnings_events/2026.parquet (the same universe the h20260922_01_earnings_text pipeline used). Horizon: next 5 trading days (matches the source's 5-day holding period). This pilot makes no near-term-profitability claim -- it is a go/no-go check on whether the feature carries any daily cross-sectional information at all before any CV harness or cost model is built.
existing_solution_comparison: Not invented here: LLM_Alpha (github.com/quangkhaidataka/LLM_Alpha, read in full) discloses the exact formula, data sources, and OOS result (Sharpe +0.78 net of 5bp, 2022-2024) for this construction, built from EDGAR 8-K + GDELT 2.0 news via Claude Haiku 4.5. Every input this pilot needs is already local: 8-K raw text (data/raw/earnings_text/, data/features/earnings_events/, from h20260922_01_earnings_text) and PIT-timestamped news (data/features/news_packets/, visible_at already computed) substitute for GDELT; the DeepSeek endpoint (scripts/score_earnings_text.py's existing OpenAI-compatible client, confirmed compatible per deepseek_api_openai_compatible_endpoint) substitutes for Claude Haiku. This iteration's only new work is: (1) a new DeepSeek prompt returning {polarity, magnitude} (the source's tone/guidance schema in score_earnings_text.py does not carry a separate magnitude field, so a new minimal prompt is needed, reusing the same neutralisation/retry/rate-limit machinery), (2) the short-MA/long-MA/rank feature build, and (3) the IC + placebo computation. No CV harness, no portfolio, no cost model -- those are explicitly deferred per the source's own construction only being reproduced for the feature, not the full strategy.
remaining_evidence_gap: (1) The LLM_Alpha repo's own H2-2021 hyperparameter validation gate FAILED (IR=-1.50) and was self-overridden by the author -- this project's rules explicitly forbid overriding a failed gate the way that paper did (see stop_condition and the registry's own reopening note); this pilot's stop rule is written to not repeat that override. (2) Independent verification this pass found that the repo's own citation of EMP2018 as justifying the negation ('mean-reversion convention') does not match what EMP2018 actually finds (anomaly returns are larger on news days broadly, not a sentiment-acceleration-specific reversal claim); Tetlock (2007) is a closer real precedent for a reversion mechanism, but at the market level, not the cross-sectional firm level -- so the sign convention is plausible but not independently confirmed by either cited paper; this pilot will observe both signs (report both the acceleration IC and its negation) rather than assume the negation is correct. (3) No independent third-party replication of the LLM_Alpha repo itself was found (single-author repo, self-audited only). (4) Whether OUR 8-K+news data (much sparser 2026 coverage than the source's dedicated 2020-24 GDELT financial-news pull) produces enough (ticker, day) coverage to compute a meaningful daily cross-sectional IC on one quarter is exactly what this pilot tests, not yet known.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:earnings_8k_tone_next_day (refuted): 8-K press-release TONE alone, priced at the next session's open, showed no next-day edge -- a same-day, tone-only, no-acceleration-transform test. This pilot is a different mechanism (acceleration of a polarity*magnitude score over a 5-day/20-day window, not the raw next-day tone level) and a different horizon (5 days, not 1). dir:news_attention_features (refuted, 0/48 BH-FDR passes, L-20260916-02 / H-20260916-02): count/novelty of news arrival carries no information -- that family never constructed a signed sentiment score, let alone an acceleration of one, so it does not pre-empt this direction (checked via `oc research directions check llm 8k gdelt sentiment acceleration` before starting, which returned dir:llm_8k_gdelt_sentiment_acceleration itself as status=triaged/queue-ready, not refuted). dir:high_freq_news_return_underreaction_drift (harvested, not refuted, h20260923_14_news_hf_reaction): a different mechanism (signed 15-minute price REACTION to news, not an LLM-scored polarity acceleration) on a different horizon (1 week) -- distinct feature, not re-tested here.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: This pilot computes only a feature and its IC; it authorizes no backtest, no cost model, and no order submission. If a later round builds a tradable signal from this feature, it will use this project's fixed convention (close signal -> next open fill, 10bp/20bp per side) reused from reports/research/signal-cards/library-v1-manifest.json, not a new convention invented here. DeepSeek calls: capped by the 5-hour rolling quota already built into scripts/score_earnings_text.py (429/limit-keyword detection -> stop and checkpoint); the same machinery is reused, not reimplemented, for the new polarity/magnitude prompt.
stop_condition: Stop before building any CV harness or portfolio if EITHER: (a) the daily cross-sectional rank IC of sent_accel (and of its un-negated mirror, accel) against next-5-day returns is not stable-signed across the quarter (e.g. flips sign in more than 40% of trading days, or the sign of the mean IC is not robust to dropping any single week), OR (b) the shuffled-news-across-tickers-within-date placebo reproduces >=50% of the real IC's magnitude with the same sign. Per the source's own disclosed weakness, an IC that only clears these bars by re-picking the sign, window lengths, or horizon AFTER seeing the result does not count as a pass -- the 5-day/20-day windows, 5-day horizon, and both sign conventions are fixed before any DeepSeek score is computed (see candidate-manifest.json). This mirrors, and refuses to repeat, the source's own override of its failed H2-2021 gate.

sources.claim: A market-neutral long-short portfolio whose signal (sent_accel) is built from LLM-extracted structured features (polarity, magnitude, event_type, tense, specificity, novelty) from EDGAR 8-K filings and GDELT 2.0 financial news, using the formula: raw_pol = polarity*magnitude per article; short_ma = 5-day rolling mean; long_ma = 20-day rolling mean; accel = short_ma - long_ma; score = -1*(cs_rank(accel)-0.5); smoothed = 30-day moving average (Alpha101 decay); rank-weighted dollar-neutral portfolio, GICS sector-neutralized, 5-day holding, weekly rebalance. On a point-in-time S&P 100 universe, Q1 2022-Q4 2024 OOS (753 trading days), net of 5bps round-trip cost: Sharpe +0.784, max drawdown 3.33%, beta_mkt +0.001, alpha +0.72bps/day with t-stat +1.345 (below 1.96 significance), 9/12 positive quarters. The frozen hyperparameter configuration failed its own pre-registered H2-2021 validation gate (IR=-1.50) and was carried forward via an author-documented override.
sources.market_and_period: Point-in-time S&P 100, WRDS CRSP + EDGAR 8-K + GDELT 2.0 news, 2020-07 to 2024-12 (feature buffer 2020-07..2020-12, hyperparameter dev 2021, OOS eval 2022-01..2024-12).
sources.applicability: This is the exact construction dir:llm_8k_gdelt_sentiment_acceleration is named for: sent_accel = -1*(cs_rank(short_ma(polarity*magnitude,5) - long_ma(polarity*magnitude,20)) - 0.5), rank-weighted, 5-day hold, purge(5)+embargo(5) CV. Pilot T-16 reproduces only this feature-construction formula on our own 8-K text scores + Alpaca/Benzinga news via DeepSeek in place of the source's Claude Haiku 4.5.
sources.limitations: Single-author repo (PhD student side project), not peer reviewed; author's own H2-2021 hyperparameter validation gate FAILED (IR=-1.50) and was self-overridden rather than passed; OOS alpha t-stat (+1.345) is below the 1.96 significance threshold; WRDS CRSP inputs are subscription-gated and not reproducible by us (we substitute our own PIT universe and SIP bars); repo cites the negation rule as the 'Engelberg-McLean-Pontiff (2018) mean-reversion convention' but the actual EMP2018 paper (see engelberg_mclean_pontiff_2018_abstract_and_finding below) does not state a sentiment-acceleration-reversal rule -- it finds anomaly returns are larger on news days, not that sentiment acceleration reverses; this is the repo author's own extrapolation, not a claim in the cited paper, and the mismatch is now recorded rather than repeated as if EMP2018 said it directly.
sources.independent_replication: No independent third-party replication of this exact repo found; the audit table in section 6 of the README (66/66 pytest cases, look-ahead/purge/PIT-universe/cost-realism checks) is the author's own self-audit, not third-party verification.

sources.claim: Using a sample of 97 stock return anomalies, Engelberg, McLean and Pontiff (2018) find that anomaly returns are 50% higher on corporate news days and six times higher on earnings announcement days; results are most consistent with anomaly returns reflecting biased expectations that are at least partially corrected upon news arrival, rather than dynamic risk or pure data mining.
sources.market_and_period: US common stocks, 97 stock return anomalies, sample period ending circa 2013 (Journal of Finance 2018 publication, working paper dated 2017-07-27).
sources.applicability: Independent check on the LLM_Alpha repo's attribution: EMP2018 is the paper the repo cites to justify negating the sentiment-acceleration signal as a 'mean-reversion convention'; reading the actual abstract shows the paper's finding is that anomaly returns concentrate on corporate-news and earnings-announcement days (consistent with biased expectations corrected on news arrival), not a sentiment-acceleration-specific reversal rule -- a real but different mechanism.
sources.limitations: Working-paper PDF (2017-07-27), not the final published Journal of Finance 2018 typeset version; page/volume citation (73(5), 1971-2001) taken from the repo's own reference list and Wiley's public listing, not independently re-verified against a paywalled publisher copy this pass.
sources.independent_replication: This is itself the original paper; not a replication. Its own within-paper tests (dynamic risk vs mispricing vs data-mining) are the authors' robustness checks, not a third-party replication.

sources.claim: High media pessimism predicts downward pressure on stock market prices followed by a reversion to fundamentals, and unusually high or low pessimism predicts high trading volume; evidence is consistent with noise/liquidity trading rather than media content as a proxy for new fundamental information.
sources.market_and_period: US stock market, daily Wall Street Journal 'Abreast of the Market' column content, sample through the mid-2000s (Journal of Finance 62(3), 1139-1168, 2007).
sources.applicability: More directly supports a sentiment-reversal mechanism than EMP2018 does: high media pessimism predicts downward price pressure FOLLOWED BY a reversion to fundamentals -- the closer real precedent for treating a sentiment extreme/acceleration as a reversal (not continuation) signal, which is what T-16's candidate feature and its negation sign convention are actually testing.
sources.limitations: Sample is WSJ column-level aggregate market sentiment (not firm-level, not LLM-extracted, not 8-K/news-specific); this is a market-wide timing result, not a cross-sectional stock-picking result, so it supports the sign/mechanism plausibility only, not the specific cross-sectional construction.
sources.independent_replication: Original paper; widely cited (this pass did not re-run an independent replication), used here only as supporting mechanism evidence, not as the tested construction itself.

sources.claim: Presents explicit formulas (also usable as computer code) for 101 real-life quantitative trading alphas built from cross-sectional rank, time-series, and decay operators; average holding period 0.6-6.4 days; average pairwise alpha correlation 15.9%; returns are correlated with volatility but show no significant dependence on turnover.
sources.market_and_period: US equities, WorldQuant proprietary alpha universe; average holding period 0.6-6.4 trading days across the 101 alphas.
sources.applicability: Source of the 'Alpha101-style rank-weighted, cross-sectional-rank, decay/ts_mean-smoothed' construction grammar (cs_rank, ts_mean/decay operators) that both the LLM_Alpha repo and T-16's own feature/portfolio-weight construction reuse verbatim rather than inventing a new weighting scheme.
sources.limitations: The 101 alphas themselves are WorldQuant proprietary trading signals disclosed for research purposes; this paper does not itself contain any LLM, news, or 8-K text signal -- it is cited only for the rank-weighting/operator convention, not as evidence for the sentiment-acceleration mechanism.
sources.independent_replication: Widely reused operator library in the public quant-finance literature and open-source alpha zoos (e.g. Alpha101 implementations); not independently re-verified line-by-line this pass.

sources.claim: GDELT is described by its own project as the largest, most comprehensive, and highest-resolution open database of world news media, monitoring print, broadcast, and web news in over 100 languages, from January 1 1979 to the present, with daily updates.
sources.market_and_period: Global news media monitoring, over 100 languages, January 1 1979-present, daily updates.
sources.applicability: Confirms GDELT is a free, open news-monitoring database (the news-source half of the LLM_Alpha construction); our own pilot substitutes our locally-held Alpaca/Benzinga news_packets store (already point-in-time timestamped) for GDELT rather than pulling GDELT directly, since the construction only requires timestamped financial news text, not GDELT specifically.
sources.limitations: GDELT's own about page is a marketing/overview page, not a technical data dictionary; it does not itself disclose per-article financial-news filtering methodology (the LLM_Alpha repo did its own GDELT financial-news filtering and deduplication to 2,908 articles).
sources.independent_replication: GDELT is an established, widely-used open dataset (used across many academic and industry projects); not independently re-verified for this specific claim beyond reading the official page.

sources.claim: Purging and embargoing (Lopez de Prado's terminology) both involve removing some of the data points near the boundaries of affected cross-validation folds in financial time series, to prevent training data whose label window overlaps a test-set label from leaking information across the train/test boundary.
sources.market_and_period: N/A -- methodology reference; the underlying method (Lopez de Prado 2018) was developed for financial time series with overlapping labels.
sources.applicability: This pilot deliberately does NOT build the full purge(5)+embargo(5) walk-forward harness the LLM_Alpha source used -- it only checks the feature's raw daily cross-sectional IC on one quarter first, per the direction's own decision rule ('stop before building the full harness if the pilot IC is not stable-signed'). This source documents what that deferred, heavier validation step would be, so the omission is a scoped decision, not an unawareness of the standard.
sources.limitations: Third-party (QuantInsti) blog explainer of Lopez de Prado's purged/embargoed k-fold CV, not the primary book text (Advances in Financial Machine Learning, 2018, is not freely accessible and is not quoted or redistributed here) -- used only as a plain-language definition to document the deferred, heavier validation step this pilot does not build, not as the authoritative source for a specific numeric parameter.
sources.independent_replication: QuantInsti is a third-party educational provider, independent of De Prado; the underlying method itself has multiple independent open-source implementations (e.g. mlfinlab) not individually re-verified this pass.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Score 2026 Q2 8-K text (h20260922_01_earnings_text universe) and same-quarter Alpaca/Benzinga news for the same tickers via DeepSeek {polarity, magnitude}; build raw_pol=polarity*magnitude per item, aggregate per (ticker, day) using each item's visible_at (filing acceptance_utc or news visible_at, whichever is the PIT timestamp), compute 5-day and 20-day rolling means, accel = short_ma-long_ma, score = -1*(cs_rank(accel)-0.5); compute daily cross-sectional rank IC vs forward 5-trading-day return; run the shuffled-news-within-date placebo.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: Mean daily rank IC has a stable sign (t-stat magnitude and sign consistent with at least 60% of individual days sharing the mean's sign) AND the placebo's mean IC magnitude is < 50% of the real IC's magnitude.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: IC sign is not stable across the quarter, or the placebo reproduces >=50% of the real IC's magnitude with the same sign -- in either case the direction is marked continue=false for this construction and not advanced to a CV harness.
